messages.subject: Unexpected result
parts:
Hello everyone,
I'm currently testing a model. The fit is good and overall the results are "interesting". However, I have an “outlier” which is contrary to what is expected from a theoretical point of view. What's more, I have several variables that are highly correlated (from 0.6 to 0.8), and I've tried to indicate this with covariances. As a result, I'm not at all sure of my results. I don't know whether to accept this "outlier" relationship, which is contrary to the literature, or whether I've overlooked something. Can anyone help me?

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected result
parts:
Hi,

A result contrary to theory is an important result, unless you have reason to suspect that there was a problem in data collection.
It is still not clear what is your problem. Is it because CALCF~SEPCF and JCCF~SEPCF have estimates greater than 1?

If so, it is probably a reflection that SEPCF have a higher variance than the remaining variables. If you want to compare its strength with the other variables, it is more appropriate to compare the std.all column.

Best,
Yago

​
